Lotus MCMC Line Painting Demo

This vignette demonstrates the MCMC line painting algorithm applied to a beautiful lotus flower image. The algorithm will run for 100,000 iterations to create a high-quality artistic interpretation.

Load the Package 

# Load the mcmcPainter package
library(mcmcPainter)

Load and Display the Target Image 

# Load the lotus image
image_path <- "../inst/extdata/lotus.png"

# Display the target image
if (file.exists(image_path)) {
  # Load and display the image
  img <- png::readPNG(image_path)
  plot.new()
  rasterImage(img, 0, 0, 1, 1)
  title("Target Lotus Image")
} else {
  cat("Image not found at:", image_path, "\n")
}

Run MCMC Line Painting 

# Run the MCMC line painting algorithm
# Note: This is a long-running process (several hours for 100,000 iterations)
res <- run_line_painter(
  image_path = image_path,
  max_dimension = 1200,
  iters = 100000,
  out_dir = "../inst/results/lotus_line_painting_100k",
  seed = 42,
  auto_config = TRUE,
  save_every = 5000,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Create Triptych Visualization 

# Create a triptych showing the progression
triptych_path <- create_triptych(
  image_path = image_path,
  result = res,
  out_path = "../inst/results/lotus_line_triptych.png",
  max_dimension = 1200
)

Display Results 

# Display the final triptych
if (file.exists("../inst/results/lotus_line_triptych.png")) {
  triptych <- png::readPNG("../inst/results/lotus_line_triptych.png")
  plot.new()
  rasterImage(triptych, 0, 0, 1, 1)
  title("Lotus MCMC Line Painting Triptych")
} else {
  cat("Triptych not yet created. Run the MCMC algorithm first.\n")
}

Algorithm Details

The MCMC line painting algorithm uses the following approach:

  1. Initialization: Start with a white canvas
  2. Iterative Process: For each iteration:
    • Birth Move: Add new lines based on image residuals
    • Death Move: Remove existing lines
    • Jitter Move: Perturb line parameters (position, color, opacity, thickness)
    • Swap Move: Reorder line rendering for better composition
  3. Acceptance: Accept or reject moves based on likelihood improvement
  4. Adaptive Temperature: Gradually increase acceptance rate over time

Performance Notes

  • Iterations: 100,000 steps for high-quality results
  • Save Frequency: Every 5,000 iterations
  • Canvas Size: Automatically scaled to 1200px maximum dimension
  • Expected Runtime: Several hours on modern hardware

Results Interpretation

The final triptych will show: - Left Panel: Initial white canvas - Middle Panel: Best MCMC result after 100,000 iterations - Right Panel: Original target image

This allows for easy comparison of the algorithm’s performance and artistic interpretation quality.
